original_question: Let G be a 3-connected cubic graph with a blue-red vertex coloring. Write B and R for the subgraphs induced by the blue and red vertices. A crumby coloring is one with maximum degree Delta(B) <= 1, minimum degree delta(R) >= 1, and no path with 3 edges in R. Since the original conjecture asserting that every 3-connected cubic graph has such a coloring is false, what relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph R is sufficient to guarantee that every 3-connected cubic graph admits a blue-red coloring of this type?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.1 in the "Crumby colorings" section: the paper asks for a relaxation of the conditions on the red induced subgraph that would make the desired blue-red coloring exist for every 3-connected cubic graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient class (3-connected cubic graphs), the fact that the coloring is a blue-red vertex coloring, the induced-subgraph notation B and R, the three defining crumby conditions Delta(B) <= 1, delta(R) >= 1, and exclusion of a 3-edge path in R, and the motivating fact that Thomassen's original conjecture is false. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
missing_details: The universal quantifier should be explicit: the sought relaxation is one that works for every 3-connected cubic graph G, not just for a fixed graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

It should be stated outright that B and R are the induced subgraphs on the blue and red vertex classes of a vertex coloring of G; in the paper, this is supplied by the sentence immediately preceding Problem 1.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

The blue-side requirement Delta(B) <= 1 should be identified as unchanged; the paper's open problem asks specifically for a relaxation of the conditions on R. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

To be fully stand-alone, the phrase "no path with 3 edges" should be retained as an explicit structural condition on R rather than left implicit through the term "crumby coloring." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

The item is an open problem in the paper, so the refined version should ask for such a relaxation rather than suggest that the paper already provides one. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
refined_question: Let G be a 3-connected cubic graph, and let V(G) = V_B union V_R be a blue-red vertex coloring with B = G[V_B] and R = G[V_R]. Thomassen's original crumby-coloring requirements are that Delta(B) <= 1, delta(R) >= 1, and R contains no path with 3 edges, but this stronger statement is false in general. Which weakening of the two red-side conditions on R is sufficient to ensure that every 3-connected cubic graph admits such a coloring while the blue-side condition Delta(B) <= 1 is kept unchanged? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
justification: The nearest official target is Problem 1.1 itself, not a broader neighboring conjecture. In Section 1, the paper first recalls Thomassen's original blue-red coloring conditions, then states that the conjecture is false, and immediately asks what relaxation of the conditions on R would recover an always-existing coloring for 3-connected cubic graphs. Your draft is already very close, so the main refinements are to make the quantifier over all such graphs explicit, restate the induced-subgraph notation in full, and emphasize that only the red-side conditions are to be relaxed while Delta(B) <= 1 remains fixed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
